frequencyClasses.per-frame-per-pair: every server frame for every observer x target pair (O(N^2) per frame)
frequencyClasses.high-rate-network: per incoming client packet at high rate (e.g. voice: 100 packets/s per speaker, times receivers)
frequencyClasses.per-action: per discrete player/game action (shot, interaction, pickup)
frequencyClasses.never-fired: declared in LabAPI, but nothing calls its dispatcher: no call site in the game build and none in LabAPI itself, so subscribing does nothing

meta.hotDefinition: hot = the frequency class is per-frame, per-frame-per-pair or high-rate-network (more than ~100 raises/s at 60 players, or once per frame): derived from the frequency, never set by hand
meta.burstDefinition: burst = raised once per shot, bullet hit, hitmarker or damage application: the rate follows the fire rate, so it spikes in a firefight and is idle otherwise; all such events are classed alike
meta.conditionallyHotDefinition: conditionallyHot = the row has hotConditions: normally cheap, but the listed situations raise it per frame (see hotConditions)

fields.settable: public properties of the args object that a handler can assign (IsAllowed included); a ref-returning property such as Message is edited in place
fields.ignoredSetters: setter names the game ignores ALWAYS: assigning them never has an effect. Every name is also in settable. scpsl-lint SL003 reports assignments to these
fields.conditionallyIgnoredSetters: [{setter, when}]: setters the game ignores only in the situation described by 'when' (a different handler object, a particular channel, one call site). Every setter is also in settable. scpsl-lint reports an assignment to one of these as SL003 at info severity and quotes the condition; read the condition before relying on the setter
fields.pair: null, or {event, role}: the partner event of the same action, role = 'before' for the -ing event raised ahead of the action, 'after' for the -ed event raised once it happened. Always symmetric: if A.pair is {B, before} then B.pair is {A, after}. Null when the row has no single before/after partner (lifecycle counterparts such as Joined/Left, intermediate stages, events whose partner does not exist)

If a handler cancels, the player is never registered, so the event RE-FIRES every frame per hazard per such player until they leave the area (becomes per-frame-per-pair while cancelled). Without cancelling it fires once per entry. Subclass overrides filter first (inactive hazard, SCPs, IgnoredTargets for PrismaticCloud, Scp939 team check) so the event only fires for eligible players, but PrismaticCloud enables its effect on the player BEFORE calling the base OnEnter, so cancelling EnteringHazard does not stop its effect. Also the pair EnteredHazard is missing for PrismaticCloud.

events.consumption: PocketCorroding teleports the player and captures the position only when allowed.
events.notes: Cancel only skips the teleport and CapturePosition; the PocketCorroding effect itself is ALREADY enabled (this runs inside Enabled, triggered by ForceIntensity), so the player keeps the corroding effect (damage ticks in Update) without being moved. To truly prevent entry cancel the EffectUpdating event or remove the effect. Not raised for non-FPC roles or when the Pocket room is missing.

events.consumption: n/a (post-event)
events.notes: Raised right after the game calls ServerSetRole with RoleChangeReason.Escaped, with NO check that the role change actually happened: if a ChangingRole handler cancelled it, Escaped still fires and the player remains in the old role. NewRole is the requested role, not necessarily the actual current role.

raisedFrom: Escape.ServerHandlePlayer (called per player from a StaticUnityMethods.OnUpdate delegate)
events.consumption: When allowed, Escape takes NewRole and EscapeScenario from the args and only acts when EscapeScenario is not None.
events.notes: HOT while players stand in the escape zone: the game's per-frame update delegate loops ALL hubs every frame and ServerHandlePlayer raises Escaping for every player for whom CanEscape is true (an FPC role, including SCPs and spectator-like FPC roles, inside an escape zone), even when the computed scenario is None, so the handler is called every frame for those players although nothing will happen. Gate cheaply on EscapeScenario not being None before doing work. Setting EscapeScenario to None makes the event a no-op even with IsAllowed true. Setting NewRole to a value while the scenario stays valid changes the role granted. Fires for dummies. The zone is small, so the total rate is (players in zone) x server frame rate, typically well under 100/s but unbounded if many camp the surface. The delegate runs once per rendered server frame over all hubs; the escape zone list is mutable and CanEscape only needs an FPC role inside one of its bounds, so the event also fires every frame for FPC players whose scenario is None (the game returns None for a role that has been active under 10 seconds and for non-Human roles). SELF-INFLICTED PER-FRAME ESCAPE: if a handler cancels a player who has a valid scenario, nothing removes them from the zone, so the event refires every frame for the whole stay. Worse, if Escaping is allowed but PlayerEvents.ChangingRole cancels the ServerSetRole call, the player stays in the zone and the sequence escape message, achievements hook and Escaped event repeats EVERY FRAME. Allocation: a PlayerEscapingEventArgs is built per player per frame before the event even when no handler is subscribed (UNVERIFIED whether LabApi skips on an empty invocation list; the args constructor still runs). Cost is bounded by players standing in the zone, normally only a few seconds at round end.
Fires only on the allowed path, after the autosync RPC carrying the tails result was written. IsTails reflects the possibly overridden value from FlippingCoin.

events.consumption: Coin runs the flip only when allowed and uses IsTails from the args as the result.
events.notes: Raised only after the 0.6 s server cooldown (non-host owner) and the BlockedInteraction.ItemPrimaryAction check, so blocked attempts never reach the event. IsTails initial value is a fresh UnityEngine.Random roll. Cancelling does NOT restart the cooldown stopwatch (the restart happens only on the allowed path), so the event can re-fire on every client command. Owner may be a dummy.

Raised from FinalizeSetGroup, NOT from SetGroup. FinalizeSetGroup is also called directly from PlayerAuthenticationManager (just before the Joined event) and from several SetGroup branches, so GroupChanged can fire without a preceding GroupChanging. Args carry the final group (can be null).

events.consumption: ServerRoles returns when cancelled; otherwise it assigns Group from the args.
events.notes: Group may be null (= remove group), both as input and as the assigned value; replacing Group redirects the rest of SetGroup (permissions, badge colour and text). SetGroup is called on join, by RA group commands and by plugins. Host/dummy behaviour UNVERIFIED.

events.hotConditions: Per-frame per victim in the same cases as Hurting (SCP-3114 Strangled effect, MicroHID primary fire, per-tick damage-over-time effects) and once per bullet/pellet; additionally raised when ApplyDamage returned Nothing (the event is raised before the game checks the handler output).
events.notes: Fires right after the damage handler applied its damage and BEFORE the game checks the HandlerOutput, so it also fires when the output is HandlerOutput.Nothing (no HP lost) and before death handling. Same GodMode/SpawnProtected exclusion as Hurting.

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the property is reassigned to a different handler object; mutating the original handler in place still takes effect

events.hotConditions: Per-frame per victim in these cases: the SCP-3114 Strangled effect (it deals time-scaled damage every frame), MicroHID primary fire (damage every server update while firing; the broken and charged fire modes deal damage through HitregUtils), plus per-tick damage-over-time effects (Bleeding, Poisoned, Hemorrhage, Scp207, Asphyxiated, Decontaminating, SCP-244 Hypothermia) and every bullet/pellet. Steady-state baseline is low but bursts of tens to hundreds per second per server are possible; keep the handler allocation-free and early-out. Not hot by default; hot during those scenarios.
events.consumption: PlayerStats returns false when cancelled; ApplyDamage runs on the original handler that was passed in, never on DamageHandler from the args.
events.notes: TRAP: assigning a new object to DamageHandler is ignored; only mutating the SAME handler object (e.g. cast to StandardDamageHandler and change Damage) has effect, because the args hold the same reference. NOT raised when the victim has GodMode or SpawnProtected (PlayerStats returns earlier). The role's ProcessDamageHandler already ran. Attacker is null for non-AttackerDamageHandler damage. Raised per DealDamage call: each bullet/pellet hit, melee hit and DoT tick. Typical total is well under 100/s but combat bursts on a full server can exceed it, so hot=false is by static estimate only, but see hotConditions. Fires for dummies.
Only on the transition from not idle to idle. The Player is the hub that triggered idle. Not raised on idle to not idle.

events.consumption: TeslaGateController stops the idle transition for that hub when cancelled; otherwise it records the hub as the one that triggered idle.
events.notes: FixedUpdate (50 Hz default, not TPS-scaled). For each active gate with no remaining inactive time it loops all alive hubs; the event is raised for each hub in idle range until one is allowed (the check is skipped once an earlier hub was allowed). So it fires every physics step per gate that has a live player in idle range even when nothing changes, and once per in-range hub per step if handlers cancel. Allocates args each time; estimated at 50-150 args per second.
Fires right after the inspect RPC/animation is sent, same five item types as InspectingItem. Not fired for keycards (see InspectedKeycard).
Fires right after the inspect-start RPC is sent.

events.consumption: Each of the five item handlers (the SCP-1344 handler, MicroHID DrawAndInspectorModule, Scp1509Item, the firearm SimpleInspectorModule and JailbirdItem) skips the inspect when cancelled.
events.notes: Raised for 5 item types only (SCP-1344, MicroHID, SCP-1509, firearms, Jailbird). Keycards use the separate InspectingKeycard. Triggered by a client command (inspect key), gated by per-item preconditions (AllowInspect / ValidateStart / ItemUsageBlocked) before the event, so rate is bounded by client input. Cancelling skips the RPC so no animation plays.

events.consumption: KeycardItem sends the public inspect RPC only if IsAllowed
events.notes: Raised only when the client asks to START inspecting and KeycardItem is not already tracking an inspect for this serial; stop requests never raise it.

CanOpen in args is the final decision (false for lock denial and permission denial). Fires on success AND denial, so it does not mean the door moved. Not fired when AllowInteracting returned false or when InteractingDoor was cancelled in the non-lock path. In the lock-denied path it can fire without any InteractingDoor ever having been raised for that call.
Only fires when the call was allowed (default or plugin-forced), after ServerSetDestination.

Raised at the end of ServerInteract for every non-cancelled interaction, including denied ones and sub-action cancellations that abort the generator's action (e.g. a cancelled OpeningGenerator still reaches it). Not raised when InteractingGenerator was cancelled (early return). ColliderId is the original collider.
CanOpen in args = final decision. Fires for both denied and success. Not fired if InteractingLocker was cancelled.
Only fires when the candy was actually added to the bag (TryAddCandy succeeded). Args carry the final (possibly plugin-modified) values.
Fires after the button action, including after the Remove button destroyed the target (NetworkServer.Destroy), so the wrapper may be dying.

Only InvisibleInteractableToy with an InteractionDuration of 0 or less (instant interaction). Timed interactions go through the search completor (GetSearchCompletor) and do NOT raise this event. No Interacting/cancellable counterpart exists for toys.
Only when allowed; carries the new lever state. The lever sound RPC is sent before.

events.consumption: In ServerInteract the door returns when cancelled and otherwise uses CanOpen from the args; in TryResolveLock it returns false when cancelled and otherwise returns CanOpen from the args.
events.notes: Two raise sites. For locked doors (active locks and no built-in bypass) TryResolveLock raises it with CanOpen false and records that the plugin request was sent, so ServerInteract does NOT raise it a second time. For unlocked doors it is raised once with CanOpen from keycard permissions. Raised only after AllowInteracting passed. Cancelling in the lock path returns false and falls into the lock-denied branch, which fires InteractedDoor with CanOpen false. Setting CanOpen to true in the lock path bypasses the lock. Player may be an SCP or dummy.

events.consumption: ElevatorChamber sends the elevator to the next level only when allowed.
events.notes: IsAllowed is PRE-SET by the game (false when the chamber is not ready for user input or the destination door has active locks) and the event is still raised, so handlers see already-denied calls; setting IsAllowed to true force-sends the elevator even when locked or moving. The panel lookup throws before the event if no panel matches.

events.consumption: Scp079Generator restarts its cooldown and returns when cancelled; its action switch uses the original collider id, not ColliderId from the args.
events.notes: TRAP: ColliderId setter is never read back (the action is chosen from the original collider id). Raised after the per-generator cooldown and the 'generator must be open for non-door colliders' pre-check. Umbrella event: Opening/Closing/Unlocking/Activating/Deactivating fire after it for the specific action.

events.consumption: Locker returns when cancelled; CanOpen decides between opening and the denied branch.
events.notes: CanOpen initial value = result of the permission check. Raised only if the chamber exists and the element can be interacted with. Setting CanOpen to true bypasses keycard permissions. The denied branch is rate limited by a cooldown (RPC only); the event itself is raised for every request.

events.consumption: Scp330Interobject returns when cancelled; otherwise it reads PlaySound, AllowPunishment, Uses and CandyType from the args.
events.notes: All four setters are consumed. Raised only for humans who can grab items, past the take cooldown and with bag space, so no event for cooldown/full bag. Uses = candies taken this life; AllowPunishment defaults to true unless the target has godmode. Setting CandyType to None skips the grant and then InteractedScp330 does not fire.

events.consumption: ShootingTarget returns when cancelled
events.notes: Only raised for players with FacilityManagement permission; otherwise silent. Args do not expose which button was pressed.

events.consumption: The panel applies the new lever state only when allowed, using Enabled from the args.
events.notes: Only raised for the Lever collider and only when the lever is not mid-animation. Enabled defaults to the toggled state (the opposite of the current one); a handler can force either state. The Cancel button collider does not raise it.

events.consumption: When cancelled, UsableItemsController clears the current usable if ContinueProcess is false and leaves it set otherwise; when allowed it completes the use via ServerOnUsingCompleted.
events.notes: Raised from a static per-frame Update that iterates every player handler, but only once per use when the use timer elapses. TRAP: cancelling with ContinueProcess true leaves CurrentUsable set, so the event is raised AGAIN on every frame until the player switches items (which cancels the use) - becomes per-frame per player; ContinueProcess false discards the use silently. Baseline frequency is per-use, hence hot=false. UsedItem is the post-event. It sits between UsingItem and UsedItem, so it has no single before/after partner.

Two raise sites: online mode raises it at the end of authentication handling (after FinalizeAuthentication and badge processing); offline mode raises it from CmdSetNick after SetNick (in online mode that handler returns early). Role/inventory are not necessarily spawned yet (UNVERIFIED), prefer role events for gameplay setup. Whether dummies pass through either path is UNVERIFIED. Host never raises it. The lifecycle counterpart is Left, which is not a before/after pair.

ProcessJump runs from FpcMotor.UpdateGrounded every movement tick for each FPC player, but the event is raised only when the client wants to jump and both the jump speed and the multiplier are positive, i.e. once per jump. The want-to-jump flag is set from the client packet (FpcFromClientMessage). ForceJump (plugins/effects) raises it too. The speed arg is the post-multiplier vertical velocity from ProcessJump and the raw jump speed from ForceJump. Fires for dummies.
Raised right after ServerConsole.Disconnect is queued; the hub is still alive (Left follows later on OnDestroy). Reason is the final plugin-modified one.

events.consumption: BanPlayer returns false when cancelled; otherwise the kick uses Reason from the args.
events.notes: Every KickUser overload funnels into this one: the RA ban command (BanCommand), the AFK kick (AFKManager) and the friendly-fire detector (FriendlyFireDetector). Issuer is the host hub when the sender is not a player. Does NOT cover ServerConsole.Disconnect called directly (bad nickname, auth failures) nor bans (separate Banning event).

events.consumption: EnvironmentalHazard returns false (player stays in AffectedPlayers) when cancelled
events.notes: OnExit is called from UpdateTargets every Update while the player is OUTSIDE the area but still in AffectedPlayers, from OnRoleChanged, and from TemporaryHazard.ServerDestroy. TRAP: cancelling keeps the player in AffectedPlayers so the event re-fires EVERY FRAME for that player-hazard pair until allowed (per-frame-per-pair when a plugin cancels). Subclasses: Tantrum and Sinkhole call the base OnExit FIRST (event fires even for SCPs and inactive hazards; Tantrum then returns false without LeftHazard); PrismaticCloud filters (inactive, SCP, ignored) BEFORE the base OnExit so no event for those. Only IFpcRole players are iterated.

events.consumption: PocketDimensionTeleport acts only when allowed; IsSuccessful then decides the outcome (true exits the pocket dimension, false kills the player).
events.notes: Raised from OnTriggerEnter (PocketDimensionTeleport) when a player enters a teleport trigger with role ActiveTime >= 1 s, so once per trigger entry. IsSuccessful initial value is true for Exit triggers, false for Killer triggers (or after warhead detonation); flipping it inverts the outcome. Cancelling leaves the player in place; re-entering the trigger raises it again. TryExit returns before the event for non-IFpcRole hubs; TryKill has no such check. Teleport is documented as nullable (forced exit by plugin) but both game call sites pass the instance.

Raised from Unity OnDestroy of the hub for every non-local hub (not the host, but yes dummies/NPCs and hubs that never finished authentication - Left can occur without Joined). The hub is still in AllHubs/HubsByGameObjects while handlers run (it is removed afterwards), but the connection is already gone; Player.Get(hub) still works. The lifecycle counterpart is Joined, which is not a before/after pair.

Only three hazard types raise it. PrismaticCloud never does although its OnExit can raise LeavingHazard, so the pair is not symmetric. Tantrum skips LeftHazard for SCPs and inactive hazards even though LeavingHazard already fired. Also raised on role change and on hazard destroy via OnExit.

Raised from the public static Exit/Kill helpers, which can be called WITHOUT a preceding LeavingPocketDimension (plugins, other game code). IsSuccessful true = escaped, false = killed by PocketDecay. Kill raises it after DealDamage, so Hurting/Hurt come first. Exit raises it only if the hub is an IFpcRole.

Raised from FpcSyncData.TryApply (per client movement packet, FpcFromClientMessage) only when the received state differs from the module's current movement state. The server overwrites the synced movement state every frame; the state processor only changes it when the client claims Sprinting with zero stamina or while sprinting is disabled (it then becomes Walking), and the getter also validates the state (it downgrades states whose speed is 0; the SCP-939 module downgrades Sprinting to Walking when not moving forwards). An honest client already sends Walking at zero stamina, with sprint disabled or standing still, so in steady state the event fires on real transitions (walk/sprint/crouch/sneak toggles, sprint to walk when velocity drops below walk speed): a few per second per player at most. Caveats: around stamina exhaustion the client's stamina lags the server, so a short burst of consecutive packets can each flip between Walking and Sprinting (one event per packet); a modified client holding sprint at zero stamina can fire it on EVERY packet (packet rate = client frame rate; an estimate is 10-20k messages per second at 100 players); SCP-939 sprinting sideways is a possible flap (UNVERIFIED, depends on the client-side moving-forwards sync). Listing it as hot would be the worst-case reading. hot=false, but it is among the highest-rate non-hot events: cheap handlers only.
Raised right after IssueLocalMute, once per target. IsIntercom reflects the command used.

events.consumption: The mute command issues the local mute for the target only when allowed. MuteCommand issues a plain mute and IntercomMuteCommand an intercom mute; neither reads IsIntercom from the args.
events.notes: TRAP: IsIntercom setter is never read; which mute kind is applied is hard-coded by the command that raised the event. Raised once per target of an RA mute / intercom-mute command (loops the resolved player list). Only these two RA commands raise it; mutes issued via VoiceChatMutes directly, and unmute commands, raise nothing here. Issuer is the host hub when the sender is not a player.

Raised after the Open flag and the cooldown were set, in the branch where the Open flag is now set. Opens done through other means (e.g. wrapper setters) bypass ServerInteract and do not raise it (UNVERIFIED).

events.consumption: Scp079Generator plays the denied animation when PlayDeniedAnimation is set, then stops when the event is cancelled.
events.notes: Raised only when the generator is Unlocked and currently closed (door toggle path), after InteractingGenerator allowed. PlayDeniedAnimation defaults to false (set by the LabAPI args constructor) and is read BEFORE IsAllowed, so it works whether or not you cancel. Locked generators go through UnlockingGenerator instead.
Fires after ammo was added; AmmoPickup is nullable (the pickup may be destroyed when the whole stack was taken). AmmoAmount is the plugin-adjusted amount.
BodyArmorItem is nullable in args; the item returned by ServerAddItem is cast to BodyArmor and may be null if the add failed.
Item is the ItemBase returned by ServerAddItem (null if the inventory refused - UNVERIFIED). The pickup is already destroyed for generic items.
Bag may be null if ServerProcessPickup produced none (it is initialised to null). The pickup may be destroyed (empty) or remain with leftover candies.

events.consumption: AmmoSearchCompletor releases the pickup (marks it no longer in use) and returns when cancelled; otherwise it uses AmmoAmount from the args.
events.notes: AmmoAmount is consumed: it drives the destroy-versus-partial decision and is added to the player's current ammo. Setting it above the clamped default can exceed MaxAmmo (no re-clamp seen in Complete; the CurrentAmmo setter was not read, UNVERIFIED). Raised at search COMPLETION (after the hold timer), preceded by SearchedPickup.

events.consumption: ArmorSearchCompletor releases the pickup and returns when cancelled.
events.notes: Raised at search completion, after SearchedPickup. The currently worn armor is dropped only after the event is allowed. Distinct from SearchingArmor (its start validation, which can also cancel).

events.consumption: ItemSearchCompletor and Scp244SearchCompletor release the pickup (mark it no longer in use) when cancelled.
events.notes: Generic item pickups plus SCP-244 deployables. Ammo, armor and SCP-330 have their own events. Raised at search completion, not at start (start is SearchingPickup). Cancelling returns the pickup to the world, no longer marked in use.

events.consumption: Scp330SearchCompletor releases the pickup and returns when cancelled
events.notes: Candy-bag pickups only (Scp330Pickup); raised after SearchedPickup. Cancel leaves the candies on the ground.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable). RaycastStart has a public setter but nothing reads it back: the RPC was already queued before this event is raised
events.notes: Fires only if PlacingBlood was allowed, after SendRpc. Player = victim, Attacker = owner. Values reflect any PlacingBlood mutation. RaycastStart setter is a trap.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable). DecalType has a public setter but nothing reads it back: the RPC was already queued before this event is raised
events.notes: Fires after the ImpactDecal RPC is queued, only when PlacingBulletHole allowed; same frequency/borderline-hot reasoning (glass = 2 per hit). DecalType setter is a trap.

events.consumption: When allowed, ImpactEffectsModule sends the blood RPC using HitPosition and RaycastStart from the args (the RPC writer captures them).
events.notes: Called from ServerProcessHit only when damage was dealt, bleeding is not disabled in the server settings and the collider is a HitboxIdentity: once per damaging bullet/pellet hit on a player (shotgun = several per shot). Args: Player = the VICTIM (the hitbox's target hub), Attacker = firearm owner. Cancelling only suppresses the visual blood RPC to clients; damage was already applied before this runs. Fires for dummies as victim/attacker. Not hot: needs a damaging hit, comparable to the Hurt rate.

events.consumption: When allowed, ImpactEffectsModule sends the decal using HitPosition and RaycastStart from the args. DecalType is never read back: the RPC writes the original decal type.
events.notes: Called from ServerProcessHit: once per bullet/pellet that hits world geometry (collider without IDestructible), and TWICE per hit on glass (the glass layer produces two decals). Never fires for hits on players (that is PlacingBlood). Player = firearm owner (may be a dummy). Rate = shots-that-hit-the-world: automatic weapons ~10/s per shooter plus shotgun pellets, so a 60-player firefight can plausibly exceed ~100/s (UNVERIFIED, derived from fire-rate reasoning, not measured) - borderline hot. Args object is allocated per hit even without subscribers. DecalType setter is silently ignored.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters; the args class does not implement IPlayerEvent)
events.notes: Fires right after the connection request is accepted, when PreAuthenticating was allowed and CanJoin true; NOT fired for rejected connections. Only a transport connection exists: no ReferenceHub/Player yet, and the client may still fail the later authentication handshake or disconnect. The ConnectionRequest has already been accepted so rejecting through it is too late.

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the event is cancelled, because CanJoin is only read when IsAllowed stays true
IsAllowed stays true, because the rejection payload is only used when the event is cancelled
IsAllowed stays true, because the force flag is only used when the event is cancelled

events.consumption: When cancelled the transport rejects the connection: it uses CustomReject when set, otherwise it sends the forced rejection (reject code 4). When allowed it accepts the connection if CanJoin is true and otherwise rejects it with the plain reject code (1). The offline branch behaves the same.
events.notes: Raised on the LiteNetLib connection-request path, once per incoming connection attempt that passed earlier checks (rate limits, ban lookup, token/signature validation, blocked countries run BEFORE it; their early returns skip the event). No Player/ReferenceHub exists yet: args carry UserId, IpAddress (real IP from the proxy header when present), Expiration, Flags, Region, Signature, ConnectionRequest. In offline mode UserId is the empty string and the IP ban check happens first. CanJoin is pre-seeded from whether the server is full (true when there is room), so a handler can set CanJoin to true to bypass the full-server rejection (slot reservation). Cancelling without CustomReject sends the forced reject (code 4); prefer the Reject*/RejectBanned/RejectCustom/RejectDelay/RejectRedirect helpers on the args, which set CustomReject and cancel the event. Handlers run inline in the connection-accept path: keep them fast and exception-free. Which thread runs it is UNVERIFIED.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised only when the switch falls through to the end. Many branches end early (attack on cooldown or blocked, AttackPerformed while charging which ends right after JailbirdServerAttack, Inspect cancelled by InspectingItem, attacks disallowed through AllowAttack), and then NO Processed event fires, so Processing/Processed are not strictly paired. Message is the possibly rewritten one.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires only on fall-through; early exits (cooldown, no attack triggered, blocked attack, Inspect cancelled) skip it, so not paired 1:1 with Processing.

events.consumption: When cancelled the handler returns. Otherwise it takes Message, AllowAttack and AllowInspect from the args, and returns if AllowInspect is false.
events.notes: Network command handler: one per Jailbird command message from the owner's client (AttackTriggered, AttackPerformed, ChargeLoadTriggered, ChargeStarted, ChargeFailed, Inspect). Only when the item is equipped and not broken (early return before the event). Message is re-dispatched in the switch, so a handler can rewrite the message type. Gotcha: setting AllowInspect to false blocks ALL messages, not only Inspect; AllowAttack gates attack/charge branches. Defaults derive from BlockedInteraction ItemUsage/ItemPrimaryAction. Rate = human input, not hot. Server-originated charge expiry (the charge update calls JailbirdServerAttack directly) does not go through this event.

events.consumption: When cancelled the handler returns; otherwise it takes Message, AllowAttack and AllowInspect from the args.
events.notes: Network command handler for SCP-1509 (AttackTriggered/AttackPerformed/Inspect), only when equipped. Unlike the Jailbird there is no global AllowInspect gate: AllowInspect only guards the Inspect case, AllowAttack the attack cases. Human-input rate.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no property setters); TargetBuilder is the live per-line StringBuilder that is appended to the main list right after the call, so in-place edits ARE honoured
events.notes: Fires per listed player after its line (prefix, badges, body) was appended to the per-player builder, only when AddingPlayer allowed. Player is the RA requester, obtained with Player.Get(CommandSender); the args declare it non-null, but it is null when the sender is not a PlayerCommandSender.

events.consumption: When allowed, RaPlayerList builds the player's line from Prefix, InOverwatch, IsMuted and Body in the args; when cancelled the line is dropped.
events.notes: Once per listed hub per RA player-list request (inner loop over players, DedicatedServer/Unverified hubs skipped), after RequestingRaPlayerList. Cost = requests x players; the RA client refreshes the list while the panel is open (interval UNVERIFIED), so a heavy handler is multiplied by player count; not per-frame. Target = listed hub. TargetBuilder is the shared per-line scratch builder, empty at this point. Cancelling drops that player's whole line from the list. Player is the RA requester, obtained with Player.Get(CommandSender); the args declare it non-null, but it is null when the sender is not a PlayerCommandSender.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires after the achievement message is sent to the client, only for non-host connections and while achievements are allowed. Player is declared nullable because it is built from the connection's NetworkIdentity. The server only sends the message; it does not confirm the client applied it, and does not dedupe repeated grants of the same achievement. Rare per player. Dummy behaviour UNVERIFIED.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires after items were added (ServerAddItem) and OnItemProvided invoked. Items/Ammo are returned to their pools immediately after the call: copy, never store. InventoryReset is the original flag. The previously dropped pickups are re-spawned on a LATER frame's Update (the player is queued for replenishment), i.e. after this event.

events.consumption: InventoryItemProvider returns when cancelled. Whether the inventory is reset is decided by the original method argument, never by InventoryReset from the args. Items and Ammo are get-only, but the same list and dictionary objects are used afterwards, so in-place edits ARE honoured.
events.notes: Called on every role assignment that grants a loadout (RoleChanged path, InventoryItemProvider, and the RA give-loadout command GiveLoadoutCommand). Fires for any role, dummies, escapes, respawns. Gotchas: (1) InventoryReset setter is a trap (the game uses its own value). (2) Cancelling releases the pooled collections, but the KeepItemsAfterEscaping drop of the previous inventory (earlier in the same call chain) has already happened, leaving the player with dropped items and no loadout. (3) Items/Ammo are pooled: do not keep references. Returns without the event when RoundRestart.IsRoundRestarting.

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the message's Channel is None, because the game treats the message as not audible and sends nothing regardless of IsAllowed

events.consumption: When allowed, VoiceTransceiver sends the message to the listener's connection unless its Channel is None.
events.notes: Per voice packet x per listener: ServerReceiveMessage is the Mirror handler for every VoiceMessage (Opus frames of 480 samples at 48 kHz, i.e. 100 packets per second per talking player, see SendingVoiceMessage). The game loops over all hubs and allocates a PlayerReceivingVoiceMessageEventArgs (its constructor calls Player.Get) for EVERY hub with an IVoiceRole, dummies included, even with no subscriber. With N talkers and 60 listeners that is about N x 100 x 60 raises per second. Player = the LISTENER, Sender = Speaker. Message is a ref property to a struct (no setter; edit its fields in place): editing Message.Channel changes the channel for that listener; the game pre-sets the channel from its receive validation, so a Channel of None means 'not audible' and setting IsAllowed to true is ignored then. Because the same message struct is reused across listeners in the loop, non-Channel edits may leak to following listeners (UNVERIFIED). Related, but not a before/after pair: SendingVoiceMessage, raised once per packet before the per-listener loop. Keep handlers allocation-free.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires when the reload STOPS, not necessarily when it completes: StopReloadingAndUnloading is called from OnAnimEndDetected and from OnHolstered when the item is holstered/dropped while IsReloading, and also from an [ExposedFirearmEvent] animation event. An interrupted reload therefore also raises ReloadedWeapon with no ammo change. Guarded by IsReloading, so unloads raise UnloadedWeapon instead.

events.notes: Network command from the owner's client when a reload is requested. IsAllowed is pre-filled with the game's own validation (the reload validator's verdict and no firearm module being busy), so a handler setting IsAllowed to true overrides that validation (e.g. reload a full magazine; downstream effects UNVERIFIED). Cancelling sends RequestRejected to the owner and, if the weapon is not already reloading or unloading, a Stop message. The Unload header goes to the separate UnloadingWeapon event. Human-input rate.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires right after the IssueReport background thread was STARTED, not after it succeeded; the HTTP send is asynchronous and can still fail.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires after the staff chat notification and after the webhook thread was started (async; delivery not confirmed).

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game takes Reason from the args and starts the background thread that sends the report; false skips the report and the bookkeeping.
events.notes: Server command CmdReport that reports to Global Moderation. Runs after the validity checks (ids present, no self-report) and after the ECDSA signature check, which is computed over the ORIGINAL reason: rewriting Reason makes the forwarded signature not match the reason (consequence on the GM side UNVERIFIED). Cancelling skips the cooldown bookkeeping: the last-report time and the reported-players counter are only updated when the report is allowed. Rare, player-driven. Player is the reporter, Target the reported player.

events.notes: Local report to server staff (the CmdReport branch that does not go to Global Moderation): same validity checks as the global one but WITHOUT the signature check or rate-limit bookkeeping. Cancelling returns silently: no staff-chat notification, no webhook, and no feedback line to the reporter.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no settable properties). After the event the game sends the InfoBuilder text (pre-seeded with a short placeholder prefix) to the requester and sends any clipboard texts added through SetClipboardText.
events.notes: Fires only when the RA info request's selection resolves to ZERO players: the hook for custom (non-player) RA entries. No Requesting/cancel pair; reply by appending to InfoBuilder and by adding up to 3 clipboard links. SelectedIdentifiers is the raw argument array; IsSensitiveInfo is the inverse of the game's own flag that says the requester may see sensitive info. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters). The game sends the builders' contents (clipboard and reply) after the event, so in-place edits are honoured.
events.notes: Fires after the full info text (role, HP, position, flags) is built and before it is sent; append to InfoBuilder to add lines. Target is the selected hub. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters). The game sends the ListBuilder text as the reply after the event, so in-place edits are honoured.
events.notes: Fires after every player line was appended, just before the reply is sent. Can append extra lines to ListBuilder. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters). The game sends the builders' contents (clipboard and reply) after the event, so in-place edits are honoured.
events.notes: Fires after the multi-player response and clipboard buffers are built, before sending. IpBuilder is null when the info is not sensitive and UserIdBuilder is null without User-ID permission (the game allocates them conditionally): null-check them. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: false returns without any reply. Otherwise the game reads IsSensitiveInfo, HasSensitiveInfoPerms and HasUserIdPerms from the args and then returns silently when sensitive info is requested but the requester lacks sensitive-info permission.
events.notes: Single-target RA info request. Same silent-return trap on IsSensitiveInfo versus HasSensitiveInfoPerms as the multi-player variant. Target is the selected hub. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: false returns with no reply at all (the builders go back to their pool). Otherwise the game reads IsDescending, Sorting, ViewHiddenLocalBadges and ViewHiddenGlobalBadges back from the args.
events.notes: Once per RA player-list request (the RA UI refreshes the list while it is open; interval UNVERIFIED). ListBuilder is the output builder, pre-seeded with a newline. Cancelling means the requester gets no reply at all (the list stays stale). Per-request cost grows with player count because AddingPlayer/AddedPlayer follow per hub. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

events.consumption: false returns without any reply. Otherwise the game reads IsSensitiveInfo, HasSensitiveInfoPerms and HasUserIdPerms from the args and then returns silently when sensitive info is requested but the requester lacks sensitive-info permission.
events.notes: Multi-select RA info request. Trap: setting IsSensitiveInfo to true while HasSensitiveInfoPerms is false makes the game silently return with no reply; raise HasSensitiveInfoPerms too. Setting HasUserIdPerms to true exposes User IDs to a requester without permission (privilege escalation vector). Cancelling returns without any reply. Player is the RA requester, resolved from the command sender: it can be null when the sender is not a player (for example the server console), even though the property is not annotated as nullable.

raisedFrom: CurrentRoomPlayerCache.ValidateCache (called from Update and from TryGetCurrent/TryGetLastValid)
events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Detection is polled: every frame the game looks up each player's room from their position (at most once per frame per player) and raises the event only when the detected room changes. So the event is per transition (room crossings, plus death, which clears the detected room, and positions with no room): OldRoom and NewRoom are nullable. The same check also runs when other code asks for a player's current or last valid room, so the event can fire from inside another system's call stack (keep handlers re-entrancy safe). Fires for dummies. Event rate is low (transitions only); the per-frame lookup cost is the game's own. Not hot as an event. ZoneChanged is raised right after this event, but only when both rooms are non-null and their zones differ; the two are not a before/after pair.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires after the game applied the resurrect effects (role set with RoleChangeReason.Resurrected, position override, blur) and after the SpawnResurrectParticles message was sent; RevivedPlayer already has the new role (so the role-change events for it fire BEFORE this one) and the next-resurrect time is already set. Not fired when the revive was skipped (null player or None role).

events.consumption: false returns without reviving anyone. Otherwise the game takes RespawnRole and RevivedPlayer from the args and revives only when the role is not None and a player is set.
events.notes: Raised when an SCP-1509 hit kills a player. Not raised while the resurrection cooldown is still running (the game returns before the event). RevivedPlayer is nullable and pre-seeded with the game's eligible spectator (null if none is eligible); a handler can supply one to force a revive. Setting RespawnRole to None or RevivedPlayer to null silently cancels the revive without IsAllowed being false (and the cooldown is NOT started). Scp1509RespawnEligibility.OnServer1509Kill has already run (side effect) before the event; Flamingo victims are remapped to their SCP-1507 respawn role before the event.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: The abort handler is called both when the client aborts (the player releases the button) and when the server invalidates the search session, so the event fires in both cases. Not fired on normal completion (that raises SearchedToy). Raised after the toy's own OnSearchAborted callback. It is one of the two outcomes that follow SearchingToy, not a before/after partner of it.

events.consumption: n/a (never raised)
events.notes: Declared but never raised: LabAPI defines the handler and its dispatcher, but nothing in the game build calls it, so subscribing does nothing. The game's ammo search completion raises SearchedPickup instead. Use SearchedPickup (check that Pickup is an AmmoPickup) or PickedUpAmmo.

events.consumption: n/a (never raised)
events.notes: Declared but never raised: the dispatcher has no caller in the game build, so subscribing does nothing. The game's armor search completion raises SearchedPickup, then PickingUpArmor.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires when the timed search COMPLETES, BEFORE the actual pickup events: for ammo, armor, SCP-244 and SCP-330 it is raised first, then PickingUpAmmo/PickingUpArmor/PickingUpItem/PickingUpScp330, which can still be cancelled (the cancel path resets the pickup's in-use state). So SearchedPickup does not mean the item was picked up. It is the only 'search completed' event for ammo and armor (SearchedAmmo and SearchedArmor never fire). It also fires for the escape item return and for ServerAddOrDrop, where there is no timed search.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires when the timed search completes, AFTER the toy's own OnSearched callback (that callback runs first).

events.consumption: false makes the search start validation fail, so the search never starts.
events.notes: Fires on search REQUEST start (the start validation), AFTER the base validation succeeded; the base validation raises SearchingPickup first and only continues to the game's own checks if that was allowed, so the order is SearchingPickup then SearchingAmmo, and a cancelled SearchingPickup suppresses this event. The AmmoPickup arg is the search target viewed as ammo. Not re-raised on the per-tick update validation. Also raised from non-player-initiated paths: the SCP-914 upgrade, the escape item return, and ServerAddOrDrop. Do not assume a player pressed the search key; cancelling there turns the item into a dropped pickup. The matching SearchedAmmo is never raised: use SearchedPickup or PickingUpAmmo for completion.

events.consumption: false makes the search start validation fail, so the search never starts.
events.notes: Search request start for body armor, after the base validation (SearchingPickup fires first and can already cancel). The BodyArmorPickup arg is the search target viewed as body armor. The game throws InvalidOperationException before the event for an invalid item type or ammo category. Also raised from non-player-initiated paths: the SCP-914 upgrade, the escape item return, and ServerAddOrDrop. Do not assume a player pressed the search key; cancelling there turns the item into a dropped pickup. The matching SearchedArmor is never raised: use SearchedPickup or PickingUpArmor for completion.

events.consumption: false makes the search start validation fail, so the search never starts.
events.notes: Base start validation for ALL pickup searches (items, firearms, ammo, armor, SCP-330, SCP-244): the subclasses call it first, so it precedes SearchingAmmo/SearchingArmor and also fires for those. Raised BEFORE the game's own validation (locked, disarmed, role can pick up, interaction blockers, then distance), so handlers see attempts the game would reject anyway. Not re-raised per tick. Also raised from non-player-initiated paths: the SCP-914 upgrade, the escape item return, and ServerAddOrDrop. Do not assume a player pressed the search key; cancelling there turns the item into a dropped pickup.

events.consumption: false makes the search start validation fail, so the search never starts and the toy's own OnSearching callback is not invoked.
events.notes: Search start on an InvisibleInteractableToy. Raised before the toy's own OnSearching callback and before the locked and distance checks, so attempts on locked toys fire it too. Start validation only; the per-tick update validation does not raise it.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game stores NewAttachments as the player's preference; it stores it under the weapon type from the client's message, never under the args' FirearmType.
events.notes: Network handler for AttachmentsSetupPreference (the client sends its preferred attachments per weapon, typically on join or when changing loadout). Args also carry the old attachments (read-only). Setting FirearmType is a trap: the game stores the preference under the weapon from the client's message. Player is a real connection hub (not null); a client can raise this at will (no rate limit visible in the handler).

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game sends the hitmarker to the player in Player, using Size, PlayAudio and Hitmarker from the args.
events.notes: Raised per damaging hit by about 20 callers (hitscan hit registration, explosive grenades, SCP abilities, Jailbird, MicroHID and others). Not raised for the local (host) player or for a null hub. Size is clamped to 0..2.55 BEFORE the event, but a handler may exceed it; the game scales the size into a single byte without clamping again, so an oversized value may wrap around (UNVERIFIED). Also sent to spectators of that player. Bursty in firefights (one per pellet or hit that qualifies) but not per-frame; shotguns may produce several per shot.

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the message channel is None: the game does not forward the packet even when the event is allowed

events.consumption: false drops the packet. Otherwise the game fans the (possibly mutated) message out to the receivers.
events.notes: Mirror handler for every VoiceMessage packet from each talking client. Message is a ref property without a setter: mutate its fields in place. A voice packet carries 10 ms of audio (480 samples at 48 kHz), so a speaker sends about 100 packets/s and 60 simultaneous talkers is thousands per second; with push-to-talk usually far fewer. Fires only after the cheap gates passed: the speaker is not null and matches the connection, has a voice role, passes the rate limit and the mute check, and the channel validation returned something other than None. After this event the game loops ALL hubs and raises ReceivingVoiceMessage per receiver (O(players) per packet): that is the real cost multiplier. The game caps each speaker at roughly 256 packets/s, so a client cannot exceed that. The LabAPI args object is allocated per raise (it is a class); the Player lookup for the speaker in its constructor is a dictionary lookup, not an allocation. Anything else in the handler multiplies at this rate. Changing Message.Channel here is overwritten per receiver afterwards, so channel changes are NOT honoured for receivers.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)
events.notes: Fires after the game stored the (possibly handler-modified) code; carries old and new attachments codes. Only fires if SendingAttachmentsPrefs was not cancelled.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised after the hitmarker message was sent (including to spectators); carries the final size, audio and type after any SendingHitmarker changes. Not raised for the local host player or when SendingHitmarker was cancelled.

events.consumption: Cancel handling differs per action module. Automatic and double-action: false returns silently. Disruptor: false sends a stop-firing message to clients and returns. Pump: the shot proceeds only when IsAllowed is true.
events.notes: One raise site per action module (shotgun/pump, automatic, disruptor, revolver/double-action). Does NOT cover other firearm types if any exist without these modules (UNVERIFIED). Fires per bullet-shot, the rate follows the weapon's fire rate (a full-auto weapon about 10-15/s per shooter; 60 players shooting is a few hundred/s worst case, but typically far lower). Cancel semantics differ per module: Automatic and Double return silently with the ammo and cocked state NOT consumed there (Automatic has already dequeued the request and left the cocked state untouched; Double has already toggled the cocked state and rotated the cylinder before the shot, so cancelling still consumes cock and cylinder state and desyncs client prediction); Disruptor sends a stop-firing message. Pump fires only when a queued shot is dequeued, and cancel just drops it (the dequeued request is already consumed). Dry-fire does NOT raise this event (Automatic raises DryFiringWeapon instead). Player is the firearm owner; dummies with firearms raise it as normal. For the double-action module the event is raised only on the server, but the same module also runs for the local host player.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Ordering trap: Disruptor raises ShotWeapon right after the ammo is decremented and the start-firing message is sent, BEFORE the actual projectile or hitscan (the shot itself is resolved later from the queued shot tickets), so it means shot started, not shot resolved. Automatic, Pump and Double raise it after the shot was processed with the backtracking callback; the shot may defer hit resolution (UNVERIFIED), so damage events may arrive after or before this. No info on hit target or shot count in args. Same rate as ShootingWeapon.

raisedFrom: RoleSpawnpointManager.SetPosition (spawnpoint flag unset or UseSpawnPoint false path)
events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Called from PlayerRoleManager.InitializeNewRole once per role change, only when the server is active and the new role is an IFpcRole with a spawnpoint handler. So NOT raised for Spectator, SCP-079 and other non-FPC roles. Not raised if Spawning was cancelled. Raised on both branches, so it fires even when the position was not applied (spawn flag or UseSpawnPoint false); the args carry the position that would have been used. Runs INSIDE InitializeNewRole, before the role's pooled object is set up and before the role-changed callbacks: inventory and role-dependent state may not be final, and calling ServerSetRole synchronously from the handler re-enters InitializeNewRole. Fires for dummies.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Only raised from the death path (the player-stats kill routine spawns the ragdoll, skipped when the damage handler asks to prevent it). ServerCreateRagdoll (used for SCP-3114 initial ragdolls and any plugin-created ragdolls) raises NEITHER SpawningRagdoll nor SpawnedRagdoll. Fires after NetworkServer.Spawn, so the ragdoll is live. Order in death: the ragdoll is spawned inside the kill routine, and the death event is raised after that routine returns, so SpawnedRagdoll arrives BEFORE the PlayerDeath event (UNVERIFIED).

events.consumption: false returns before any position is applied. Otherwise the game reads SpawnLocation, HorizontalRotation and UseSpawnPoint back from the args and applies the position only when the role's spawn flags include the spawnpoint flag and UseSpawnPoint is true.
events.notes: Raised once per role initialisation for FPC roles that have a spawnpoint handler (see Spawned). Setting SpawnLocation or HorizontalRotation also forces UseSpawnPoint to true and adds the spawnpoint flag to the role's spawn flags, so the position is applied even if the role change used flags without a spawnpoint; that side effect persists on the role object. Setting IsAllowed to false returns early: the player is NOT teleported and Spawned is NOT raised (the player stays at the previous position or origin). The role is already assigned and initialised when this runs. Fires for dummies.

events.consumption: false returns without spawning a ragdoll. The ragdoll data is built from the damage handler the game passed in, so the args' DamageHandler is never read.
events.notes: Death path only (see SpawnedRagdoll). Cancel returns null without a ragdoll; the kill routine ignores the return value, so the inventory drop and the change to Spectator continue. The DamageHandler setter is a trap: replacing it does not change the ragdoll's cause of death. Mutating fields of the existing handler object does work, since it is the same instance.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: EndSpin is an exposed firearm event driven by the firearm animator, not by the command handler, and has no server-only guard: it fires wherever the animation event executes. Whether the dedicated server evaluates the animator event is UNVERIFIED; if the animation does not run server-side the event may never fire, or may fire without SpinningRevolver having been allowed (e.g. a client-side-only spin). Do not use it as a guaranteed pair with SpinningRevolver.

events.consumption: false returns false from the spin attempt: no message is sent, so the spin animation is not started on clients.
events.notes: Called from the client command handler on the client request, and also publicly callable by other code (ServerTrySpin is public). Not raised when another module is busy (the game returns before the event), except for the local player.

events.consumption: The game rebuilds its list of affected hubs from AffectedPlayers; each remaining player gets the hazard's per-frame stay effect, and the pooled list goes back to its pool afterwards.
events.notes: Not cancellable and has no Player property (it implements IHazardEvent only). AffectedPlayers has no setter, but the list itself is mutable: remove entries from it to exempt players. It is a per-hazard event: the hazard update runs every frame when the server is active (temporary hazards go through the same update, so they raise it too), once per hazard instance that currently has at least one player already inside. Players who entered this very frame are not in the list (the enter effect happens first and they join the list next frame). The list is a pooled List<Player> returned to the pool right after the event: do NOT keep a reference. Removing a player from AffectedPlayers skips the stay effect for that player (tantrum slow, decontamination damage, etc.), the only effective lever. Allocation: one args object plus one pooled list rent per raise; Player.Get per affected hub is a dictionary lookup. The game returns before the event when no player is inside, so an empty hazard costs only the scan of all hubs (an in-area check per FPC hub per frame, hazards times players). Not a before/after event: the related events are EnteringHazard and LeavingHazard.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Only when the drop was a throw (a throw was requested and the DroppedItem handler ran) and the pickup has a Rigidbody. Velocity and torque are already applied when this is raised. Distinct from ThrewProjectile (grenades go through ThrowableItem). Fires after DroppingItem and DroppedItem.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Raised after the projectile is spawned and activated (the throw call runs first, then the activation call starts the fuse), so a handler that wants to alter the fuse must account for that. Args hold the projectile (ThrownProjectile; it may be null if the throw guard was hit, UNVERIFIED whether reachable), the projectile settings and the force flag as changed by ThrowingProjectile. Covers grenades, flash, SCP-018, snowballs and the like via ThrowableItem.

events.consumption: false re-adds the item to the player's inventory (the original serial is kept) and destroys the dropped pickup; true leaves the throw as it is.
events.notes: Fires AFTER the item was already dropped and after the DroppingItem/DroppedItem events; cancelling re-adds the item to the inventory and destroys the pickup (the re-add raises the item-added events again, the serial is preserved), so cancel is not a clean no-op: a drop is observed first. To block the drop entirely cancel DroppingItem instead. Only reached when a throw was requested and the pickup has a Rigidbody.

events.consumption: false sends a throw-cancelled message to the client and returns. Otherwise the game reads ProjectileSettings and FullForce back from the args.
events.notes: The camera transform has been temporarily moved to the client-supplied start pose when the event runs, and is restored only on the success path; on the cancel path the camera position and rotation are NOT restored (UNVERIFIED consequence: it stays at the client-supplied pose until the next sync). The default settings struct depends on whether the throw is a full-force one (full or weak throw settings).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: No Toggling counterpart exists, so the mode switch cannot be cancelled via LabAPI. The new mode (a single-shot flag) is read straight from the client and rebroadcast to clients BEFORE the event; the server does not validate cooldown (the 0.4 s switch cooldown exists only on the client), so a modified client can spam it. NewMode is passed raw.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Covers all ToggleableLightItemBase items (flashlight, lantern, etc.), not firearm lights (see ToggledWeaponFlashlight). Carries the final state after any TogglingFlashlight change. Raised even if the state did not actually change (a client can send the same NewState).

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Raised even when the role is not an IFpcRole: the flag is not inverted and a console message that noclip is not supported is sent, but ToggledNoclip is still raised with the unchanged flag value. Only reached when TogglingNoclip was allowed (IsAllowed is pre-seeded with the game's own noclip-permission check).

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: NewState is fixed per branch (true for enable, false for disable). Raised before the status message is sent to clients, so clients are not yet updated. Not raised for battery depletion: when the battery runs out the radio switches itself off silently, so no Toggled event fires.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: The server enforces a 0.5 s cooldown and the item-usage block. Not raised for the automatic re-enable when an attachment is removed.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game applies NewState to the item's light and broadcasts the new state to clients; false does neither.
events.notes: NewState's initial value is the state the client requested, not a toggle of the server state. Cancel means no broadcast and the requesting client may desync until the next resync (UNVERIFIED). Gated on the player holding the item with that serial.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game flips the player's noclip admin flag.
events.notes: IsAllowed is pre-seeded with the game's own noclip-permission check, so a handler can grant noclip to a player lacking the permission by setting IsAllowed to true (the game then flips the noclip flag). Fired on the client message whenever the noclip key is pressed. The NewState arg is the requested toggle.

events.consumption: false returns. Otherwise the game switches the radio on (enable branch) or off (disable branch) by itself; NewState is never read.
events.notes: NewState has a public setter, but the game hard-codes the new state in each branch, so changing NewState does nothing. The branches are only reached when the radio is currently off with battery above zero (enable) or currently on (disable). Skipped entirely while the owner has an item-usage block. The ChangeRange command raises ChangingRadioRange instead.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game applies NewState and sends the status to clients.
events.notes: NewState's initial value is the inverse of the current server state (unlike the item flashlight). Not raised when the attachment is disabled, item usage is blocked or the 0.5 s cooldown is active.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Raised once per gate activation (after the gate's server-side activation ran), with the hub that was first allowed to trigger it. The hub is the first allowed player in range, not necessarily every player who is in range. Only living players are considered.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true that player becomes the gate's trigger and the gate activates later in the same pass; false skips that player (and the same player is checked again on the next step).
events.notes: Runs in the physics step (fixed update) for every active gate that is not in its inactive period and for every ALIVE player who is in range while the gate is not already in progress. At Unity's default step of 0.02 s that is 50 times a second; the dedicated server's setting is UNVERIFIED. While a player stands in the trigger range and the handler cancels, it re-fires EVERY fixed step per such player (a cancelled trigger is retried each tick, so a cancel-everything handler on a crowded gate is hot). Also fires for non-human roles (SCPs, dummies) in range; role immunity is handled inside the range check: roles that cannot activate the shock and non-FPC roles return false before the event. The loop stops for a gate once one player was allowed, so at most one allowed trigger per gate per tick. Hot only when players are inside gate range; on an idle server: zero.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Raised after the disarmed status was cleared. Fires only on the disarm-release path of a client DisarmMessage, after the game checked the cooldown, the distance (within about 4.5 m) and that the target holds only a common-tier item. The CanUnDetainAsScp arg is false when the uncuffer is on the SCP team (SCP uncuffers cannot uncuff).

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the uncuffer is on the SCP team: the game rejects the uncuff regardless of the event result, so setting it to true cannot grant it

events.consumption: The game returns (no uncuff) when IsAllowed is false or when the uncuffer is on the SCP team; the SCP-team rejection is applied regardless of what the event set.
events.notes: Trap: even with IsAllowed set to true an SCP-team uncuffer is rejected, because the game combines the event result with its own team check; CanUnDetainAsScp is a read-only informational property and does not let a plugin grant it. The event is also not raised when the uncuffer is themself disarmed.

events.consumption: n/a

events.consumption: n/a (post-event, not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Handler name is PlayerEvents.UpdatedEffect, raised via PlayerEvents.OnUpdatedEffect. Server only. Fires only when the intensity actually changes (the game returns early when the new value equals the stored one), so repeated EnableEffect on an already-active effect (e.g. hazards re-enabling Stained every Update) raises nothing. The Intensity passed is the requested value, not the value after the game clamps it to MaxIntensity. Duration is the effect's Duration at that instant: via ServerSetState the new duration is applied only after the intensity changes, so Duration here is the OLD duration. Raised before the effect's own enabled/disabled callbacks run, so IsEnabled is already updated but subclass reactions are not. Effects that drive Intensity from per-frame logic (SCP-1576 clamps its time left each update, InsufficientLighting, SCP-1853) raise it whenever the value changes, which can be about once per second per affected player.

conditionallyIgnoredSetters.when: the change comes through ServerSetState or EnableEffect: the game applies its own duration right after the event and overwrites the handler's value

raisedFrom: StatusEffectBase.ForceIntensity (reached from the Intensity setter, ServerSetState, DisableEffect, CokeBase, Scp1853)
events.consumption: The game returns without changing the effect when IsAllowed is false. Otherwise it applies Intensity (capped at MaxIntensity) and Duration from the args; on the ServerSetState and EnableEffect paths the Duration is overwritten right afterwards.
events.notes: Fires only when the intensity actually changes (the game returns early when the new value equals the stored one) and only when the server is active, but fires for every effect type including internal ones. A pure duration refresh at the same intensity raises nothing. Disabling or expiry also raises it, with Intensity 0. TRAPS: (1) the 'became enabled' decision is taken BEFORE the event, so setting Intensity to 0 from a handler still runs the enabled callbacks with intensity staying 0, and the disabled callbacks never follow. (2) Cancelling does not stop a caller that retries every frame: Hypothermia-style effects re-set Intensity each update when enabling is not allowed, which re-fires this event every frame per such player (the rate of this event on a live server is UNMEASURED). (3) Duration given is the current (old) Duration, see UpdatedEffect. Player is the effect owner hub, may be a dummy. Server code sets Intensity from per-frame and per-tick paths, so the event is not just per-action: SCP-1576 sets Intensity from its time left every update, so it fires about once per second per SCP-1576 user while active; SlowMetabolism sets Intensity 1 or 2 every tick; SCP-1853 on danger-stack change; InsufficientLighting on light-state flips (checked per frame, event only on change). Disabling every enabled effect on death or role change sets Intensity to 0 for each, so a burst of events (one per active effect) occurs per death. If a handler CANCELS, the game returns before the new intensity is stored, so every retrying caller (the SlowMetabolism tick, SCP-1576 per frame) refires the event each tick or frame for that player: treat it as HOT once you cancel. Cancelling also skips the sync to clients and the enabled/disabled callbacks. Keep the handler O(1) and filter by the Effect type first.

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: The game loops every frame over all players, but the event fires only when a use completes. Raised after the use-completed callback ran and the current usable was cleared. Not raised when the use was cancelled (item switch) or when applying the effects was cancelled via ItemUsageEffectsApplying. Includes SCP-330 candy use (same controller).

events.consumption: n/a
events.notes: Raised every frame for EVERY radio item that is usable (switched on with battery left) and whose UsingRadio was not cancelled, on the server, including radios not currently held: the update has no held-item gate (the held check only guards the status message), so any switched-on radio in an inventory keeps draining. It therefore scales with the number of switched-on radios, e.g. 40 radios at 60 fps is 2400 events/s. Carries the drain amount applied.

raisedFrom: Intercom.CheckPlayer (called from Update in the Ready state for the first qualifying player, and in the InUse state for the current speaker)
events.consumption: false makes the player check fail (the player does not count as a speaker); true passes it. State is never read.
events.notes: Fires from the intercom update every frame while at least one human within intercom range is transmitting voice (the check short-circuits on range, human role, sending voice and not being muted, all before the event). In the Ready state the scan stops at the first player that passes, so cancelled players are re-evaluated EVERY frame (a cancel handler fires per frame per qualifying speaker); in the InUse state the current speaker is checked every frame. An idle intercom costs only the cheap pre-checks, no events. Only one intercom exists (singleton). The State arg is the current state; the check is only reached from the Ready and InUse branches, never Starting, so State is Ready or InUse in practice. Its setter is ignored. Cancel in InUse does not end the session at once: a failed check means the sustain timer is not restarted, and the session continues until the sustain time (a prefab value, UNVERIFIED) or the speech timer expires, then Cooldown and UsedIntercom. Cancelling every frame therefore does not silence instantly; to block use cancel in Ready.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game starts the use (for a usable item it records it as the current usable and sends the Start message to clients; for SCP-330 it records the selected candy); false does neither.
events.notes: Fires when use STARTS (client Start request), not when it completes; the effect is applied later (UsedItem). Raised after the cooldown and speed-multiplier checks, so a request during cooldown never reaches the event. Selecting a candy from SCP-330 raises it with the bag as the item (second raise site) and can come from the select message without a cooldown check. ServerEmulateMessage lets server code trigger it for any holder.

events.consumption: When IsAllowed is true the game takes Drain from the args and subtracts it from the battery (clamped to the 0 to 1 range); false means no drain this frame.
events.notes: Per frame per switched-on radio with battery (see UsedRadio). The default Drain scales with frame time and with the radio's range level (talking costs more than idle). Cancelling means no drain at all this frame. Setting Drain to 0 gives an infinite battery, but still costs the per-frame handler. Efficient infinite-battery alternative: keep the handler trivial (no allocations) or avoid subscribing and set the battery directly.

events.consumption: When IsVisible is false the game does not write the target's position data into the receiver's position message and reports the target as invisible to the sync-data builder; when true it writes it normally.
events.notes: Per receiver and target pair, every position tick: the position distributor sends one position message per verified connected hub at an interval of one over the server tickrate (clamped to 10..60), and building each message loops all FPC hubs (excluding the receiver and the local host). 60 players at 60 tick: about 60 x 59 x 60, roughly 212,000 raises/s. Player is the receiver, Target the observed player. IsVisible is pre-seeded from the role's ICustomVisibilityRole validator. Setting IsVisible to false hides the target's position from that receiver (invisibility plugins), true forces it visible even against the SCP-079 and SCP-3114 visibility rules. Anything beyond a dictionary lookup or flag test in this handler is a measurable cost; the args constructor does two Player.Get dictionary lookups plus one args-object allocation per pair. Receivers are every verified non-host hub (spectators and SCPs included), targets every other FPC-role hub.

Raised right after RoomChanged; the two are not a before/after pair. Fires for dummies. Can be raised from callers that ask for the player's current room, i.e. synchronously inside other code.

events.consumption: n/a

If the ragdoll was already consumed and HealIfAlreadyConsumed is false, the method returns BEFORE ConsumedCorpse fires, so Consumed does not always follow Consuming. events.consumption: The game returns Error as the start result; any value other than None refuses the start.

The event is raised even when the game already computed an error (AlreadyConsumed, TargetNotValid, FullHealth, BeingConsumed), which arrives pre-filled in Error. Target is the Target of ResurrectingBody (it may differ from the ragdoll owner). The target's own RoleChanged and Spawned events fire earlier, inside the role change.

Changing Target redirects the role change and teleport to another player (the ragdoll is still destroyed, and the 200 hume shield bonus check uses the new target). Target is built from the ragdoll's owner; if that is null (the owner left) Player.Get(null) gives null and the game would throw a NullReferenceException after the handler (UNVERIFIED path for the null case). The revived role is Scp0492, or ZombieFlamingo for an SCP-1507 ragdoll. The Player setter is a trap.

events.consumption: n/a

The damage handler notifies every 049 instance, but a check that the instance has a target and that it is the dead player means only the owner of that sense fires. Adds the target to the dead-targets and special-zombies lists (for the 200 hume bonus and the zombie variant). Fires inside ApplyDamage, i.e. possibly before the death is fully processed (Dying/Died ordering UNVERIFIED). It is a later outcome of UsingSense/UsedSense, not a before/after partner of them.

A target killed by a Scp049DamageHandler raises SenseKilledTarget instead (the target is cleared first); a target dying from other damage is dropped through the update path (it is no longer an FPC role) and raises this event. The target Player may be null if the hub was destroyed (UNVERIFIED). It is a later outcome of UsingSense/UsedSense, not a before/after partner of them.

events.consumption: false makes the game return error code 1 (target null), which is sent to the client as an error. Otherwise a false CanResurrect becomes a target-invalid error and a true one lets the start proceed.

Setting IsAllowed to false returns code 1 (ResurrectError.TargetNull), which is sent to the client as an error RPC. Target is Player? (null when the ragdoll owner disconnected). Starting is only the begin of a 7 s channel; the actual resurrection is ResurrectingBody, which is why this is not a before/after pair with it.

Replacing Target skips the line-of-sight validation (it was done for the original target), but the per-frame visibility check will drop an unseen target on the next frame and raise SenseLostTarget.

Network command handler guarded by the ability being ready and the signal not being lost; the game's else-branch sends the failure RPC only when that guard failed. On cancel no aux or cooldown is consumed and no RPC reply is sent, so the client UI gets no feedback. The room is read without a null guard for the args constructor.

events.notes: Fires after the game's checks passed (the error code is Zoom, i.e. no error). The zone comes from a client byte. Cancel means no aux cost, no cooldown, no RPC.

events.notes: Fires when the lockdown ends (timer) and also from the role reset without an active lockdown (see CancellingRoomLockdown). Fired after the doors were unlocked and the RPC sent.
