events.notes: TRAPS: (1) the update caller runs every frame while a lockdown is in effect and its remaining duration is used up, so cancelling re-fires this event EVERY FRAME until allowed (per-frame while denied). (2) The role reset calls the cancel routine unconditionally on every 079 role reset, with no check that a lockdown exists, so the event (and CancelledRoomLockdown) fires on each 079 despawn or role change even when no lockdown is active; Room (the last locked room) can then be null or stale (UNVERIFIED how Room.Get(null) behaves). (3) The natural end of a lockdown (duration elapsed) is the normal path here; there is no player-initiated cancel. The role reset only calls the cancel routine while the server is active; if a handler cancels during a role reset, the lockdown flag stays set on a role that is being reset, and nothing retries it.

Camera changes through other paths (the initial default camera, client sync) raise NO event. A player can switch several times a second, but the total is far below 100/s.

For a last-SCP target the handler is followed by a lethal damage call; the attack only aborts if that damage is refused (godmode or spawn protection), otherwise it continues to the teleport effect. events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)

events.notes: Raised from Scp173ObserversTracker.UpdateObserver, which the per-frame update calls for EVERY hub in ReferenceHub.AllHubs on every SCP-173 instance (server only). Fires on the observed to not-observed edge. TRAP: cancelling keeps the target in the observer set (173 stays frozen versus that player) and re-raises the event every frame until the target is observing again. Cancelling this is the supported way to make 173 sticky-frozen, but it costs a handler call per frame per pair.

Its doc comment claims the event fires even when the ability is not ready; this is false in 1.1.7/14.2.7 (the blink method returns false before any event when the ability is not ready). (2) Forced reveal from the per-frame update when the identity is active and the remaining duration has expired: TRAP, cancelling there re-fires the event EVERY FRAME for the rest of the disguise because the condition stays true. TRAP: cancelling the out-of-range or damage abort re-raises the event every frame (the range check runs each frame) or never completes; cancelling during ResetObject (role change) leaves a stale target. A target that died also triggers it via OnPlayerRemoved.

After a cancel in ServerProcessCmd the game still sends the RPC with an RPC type derived from the old state, so clients may briefly see an inconsistent state (UNVERIFIED visual effect).

events.notes: Per player (including dummies) found in the intake chamber at upgrade time, after a line-of-sight check to the intake chamber. The Damage override is honoured at all three. (2) The lunge cancel paths return out of the command handler: a primary cancel returns after the target was already moved to the lunge position and rotated, and BEFORE it is restored and before the state becomes LandHit, so the victim is left displaced (from reading the code; not runtime-tested). A secondary cancel aborts the remaining secondary victims AND skips the hitmarker and the LandHit state. Distinguish the sources by comparing Damage (120 or 30) or the call stack; there is no field for it. Player dummies are valid targets. In the claw path, Attacked fires even if the damage call returned false (see Attacked).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)

events.consumption: The ability only starts the hold timer and instantiates the cloud when the event is allowed.
events.notes: OnStateEnabled runs from the TargetState setter on the false to true edge (setter callers: ServerProcessCmd, ClientProcessRpc, OnKeyDown, ResetObject). The server path requires the cooldown to be ready. Cancel only skips the cloud and the hold timer: TargetState stays true and ServerProcessCmd still triggers the failed-placement cooldown; consequences for the client state machine are UNVERIFIED (normally the cloud instance confirms or fails the placement, which now never happens). Fires on every instance including clients; on a dedicated server only the server instance matters.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)
events.notes: No Focusing event exists. Raised from the TargetState setter on every change of the focus state. Driver: the server update assigns the state every frame from three conditions (ability available, key held, claw ready) and the setter only acts on a change, so the event fires at edge rate. The state is also set to false when the lunge leaves the None state. FocusState is the new value (true = focus started, false = ended). The client RPC writes the state directly, bypassing the event. Fires on the server instance; grounded flapping can produce rapid on/off bursts.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)

events.notes: Raised from the State property setter on EVERY lunge state transition, not only the start: Triggered (TriggerLunge), LandHarsh/LandRegular (OnGrounded), LandHit, None (OnFocusStateChanged, ResetObject). LungeState is the NEW state; compare it to know the phase. Also raised on clients and from ClientProcessRpc. Cancelling a None reset (e.g. ResetObject on role change) leaves a stale state. The setter returns early when the value equals the current state, so there are no duplicate events for the same state.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)

SelectedSequence is the byte read from the client and is NOT bounds-checked here; the client RPC wraps it modulo the number of sequences, so out-of-range values wrap. The cooldown is only started when allowed, so a cancelling handler lets the client spam the command (one event per request).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)
events.notes: Driven by the hume-shield stat's value change when the shield goes from above 0 to 0 or below on the server. Requires the owner to be an SCP AND the shield to have a break sound, so roles without a break clip never raise it. Fires per RA unban / banremove.

The removal uses the ORIGINAL ban Id (taken before the BanDetails override is applied), so changing BanDetails.Id in the handler leaves the old row in place. The args carry the old details.

Additionally likely DOUBLE-RAISED on the server: ServerSetTargetState calls the state-setting method directly, which assigns the synced open flag; the generated SyncVar setter then invokes the hook again because NetworkServer.activeHost is true on SCP:SL servers (Mirror), so Changing and Changed each fire twice per server-initiated change (UNVERIFIED by runtime test). Also raised once per door at spawn from OnStartClient. Few doors (at most 4), a handful of events per round.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)

NewSequence IS applied to the sync var, but CheckpointDoorSequenceChanged and OnSequenceChanged then report and use the ORIGINAL requested value, not NewSequence.

events.consumption: n/a (no args)
events.notes: Raised after the sequence flag is set, the DeadMansSequenceActiveMessage is broadcast and the warhead start is triggered, i.e. the warhead Starting/Started events (WarheadEvents) fire BEFORE this event. Triggers: the countdown elapsing in OnUpdate, the RA command "dms force" (the Dms ForceCommand) and the Hubert Moon holiday.

events.consumption: When cancelled the game resets the switch and returns.

The countdown is checked every frame in OnUpdate but the event only fires when it elapses. The args class has no properties besides IsAllowed (default true).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised after RemainingHealth was reduced but BEFORE the door is flagged destroyed and DoorEvents.TriggerAction(Destroyed) runs, so the door is not yet marked destroyed when handlers run even if this hit killed it (check RemainingHealth at or below 0).

raisedFrom: BreakableDoor.ServerDamage (callers: ExplosionGrenade, Scp096HitHandler, Scp1507AttackAbility, DisruptorHitregModule, Scp018Projectile, the MicroHID charge fire mode, DestroyDoorCommand, CheckpointDoor.ServerDamage per sub-door)

The Damage setter is consumed (it is subtracted from the remaining health). SCP-018 bouncing and 096 hits can raise it repeatedly (per bounce or hit) on non-destroyed doors; explosions raise one per door per blast. Total rate is normally below 20/s.

raisedFrom: DoorVariant.Update (per-frame poll comparing the active locks with the previous value)

events.notes: Detected by polling in DoorVariant.Update (runs every frame for every door, about 100-200 doors) but raised only when the lock bitmask changes (and not during a short post-spawn cooldown). The event fires one frame after the lock was set and carries the old and new masks; several changes in one frame coalesce into one event. Warhead start or detonation locks all elevator doors, and generators or a 079 lockdown toggle many doors at once, causing bursts of 10-100 events in one frame.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)

The initial placement raises it during Start/ServerSetDestination, and a Ready to Ready change is possible (the old value is read just before the assignment). Not cancellable; no Player (elevator movement is driven by interactions - find the rider via the chamber).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised after all overlap-sphere damage and door destruction but BEFORE the host hitboxes are switched off again. Values are the post-Spawning (plugin-modified) ones. Not raised if Spawning was cancelled. The attacker's Hub may be null.

raisedFrom: ExplosionGrenade.Explode (static; callers: ExplosionGrenade.ServerFuseEnd, ExplosionUtils.ServerExplode (SCP-018 Scp018Projectile, PinkCandy/Cola/Jailbird effects, HubertMoon), DisruptorHitregModule)
events.consumption: When cancelled the game returns before dealing damage; otherwise Position, Settings, DestroyDoors, ExplosionType and the attacker (from Player) are used.
events.notes: Broader than grenades: also pink candy, cola, jailbird, disruptor shots and SCP-018 via ExplosionUtils - the disruptor fires one per shot (rapid fire = tens per second). Cancel returns before damage AND before the host hitboxes are touched. Player may be null (the attacker hub is then null); a null Player leaves the attacker empty. The Settings setter is consumed - a null value would throw a NullReferenceException when the game reads the maximum radius.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)

events.consumption: When allowed, the generator is engaged, its activating flag is cleared and the engaged callbacks run; when cancelled none of that happens.
events.notes: TRAP: raised from the per-frame ServerUpdate while the generator is activating, not yet engaged and activation is ready. If the handler cancels, the generator stays not engaged and its timer stays at or above the total, so the event re-fires EVERY FRAME for that generator (up to 5 generators at 60 fps = 300/s) until the activation conditions lapse (someone stops, drop-down); the early return then skips the time update. Normally once per generator. Cancel only together with a state change that breaks activation readiness.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised even when the pickup is only registered for a later spawn behind a trigger door, i.e. it may not be network-spawned yet. Same burst profile as ItemSpawning.

Burst of about 100-400 events during map generation at round start (one per spawnpoint or pickup), then none. Cancelled pickups are not destroyed by this code path (orphaned un-spawned GameObject, UNVERIFIED cleanup).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable)

Raised once per announcement phase (about 6 per round). NOT raised for the final phase: the game stops updating and returns first, and that final phase sets DecontaminationOverride to Forced just before. Raised outside the block that plays an audible announcement line (which has a 10 s post-join cooldown), so it fires even for silent phases.

events.consumption: n/a (no args)

raisedFrom: DecontaminationController.FinishDecontamination (called from the DecontaminationOverride setter when the value is Forced)

Also triggered by the RA decontamination force; warhead detonation sets Disabled (no event).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised BEFORE PoolManager.RestartRound and before the OnGenerationStage phases run: rooms exist but later generation stages (item distribution, doors, lockers) may not have run. Also raised on clients in a client process, but only the server matters here.

events.notes: Cancelling (or setting Seed to -1) selects the generation-disabled seed -1: the seed message is still sent to everyone and GenerateLevel(false) skips GenerateFacility but still sets up all room connectors and raises MapGenerated. So MapGenerated fires even when cancelled. Fires at scene start (SeedSynchronizer.Start), BEFORE plugins' round state exists for the new round; the Seed from the map_seed config or random is already chosen. The game does not clamp a plugin-supplied Seed (only its config path).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)

events.notes: Influence is the NEW ABSOLUTE value (current plus delta), not the delta; a handler computes the delta from the current value. Raised on every objective completion (even with 0 influence, e.g. a generator without SCP-079) and by RA wave commands. Cancelling also skips the InfluenceModified delegate that drives the RespawnTokensManager milestones. Also executes outside the server-active guard (the Modified event is inside it).

A pickup instantiated by ItemDistributor.ServerCreatePickup but then cancelled in ItemSpawning is never network-spawned yet still gets Start and this event (UNVERIFIED that Unity runs Start on an un-spawned instance; the object is active, so it should). Burst of hundreds at round start (item distributor); frequent in fights and deaths. Skipped if the wrapper is already in Pickup.Dictionary. Raised on the main thread. The lifecycle counterpart is PickupDestroyed, which is not a before/after pair.

The pickup wrapper comes from a dictionary lookup: if the wrapper was never registered, Pickup is NULL in the args (the args constructor accepts a possibly-null item). The wrapper is removed (OnRemove) BEFORE the event, so wrapper state may be partially torn down. Also fires for pickups consumed by players (picked up, then destroyed). The lifecycle counterpart is PickupCreated, which is not a before/after pair.

The Position setter actually MOVES the projectile transform before detonation. Player (thrower) may be null, in which case the attribution is cleared. Fires for frag, flash, SCP-018 and SCP-2176 (all TimeGrenade subclasses), not for SCP-244 or other pickups.

Setting CanEnd to true triggers RoundEnding next, in the same iteration. The SCP keep-alive extra targets are already inside the vanilla value.

events.consumption: n/a (no args)

events.consumption: n/a (no args)

Role assignment is driven by RoundStart.RoundStartTimer; players may not have roles yet when this fires (UNVERIFIED ordering versus role selection).

With round-autostart scenes (non-facility) the single call is not retried.

events.consumption: When cancelled the sender gets the reply "A server plugin cancelled the message." and nothing is sent; otherwise the Message override is used.

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised after logging and fan-out to all hubs holding the admin-chat permission; carries the final (possibly plugin-modified) message.

events.consumption: n/a (no args)
events.notes: Guarded by a quitting flag, so it fires once per process. Fires AFTER Shutdown.OnQuit and BEFORE ServerShutdown.Shutdown/InternalShutdown: players are still connected, but there is only a window of about 0.6-2 s (InternalShutdown waits at most 20 times 100 ms), so do not do slow I/O.

events.consumption: n/a (no args)
events.notes: Raised from Start of the local-player CharacterClassManager, guarded by isLocalPlayer and NetworkServer.active, so once per scene load / round restart, immediately before the Init coroutine (lobby countdown). RoundStarted follows later. All LabAPI events go through EventManager.InvokeEvent, which wraps each subscriber in its own try/catch: one throwing handler does not stop the others, and for cancellable events every handler runs even after IsAllowed was set to false (last writer wins).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: The Players list is built from the INTENDED spawn set, not from the players actually spawned: players beyond the maximum wave size, or whose role assignment threw, are still included. Fires after the roles are set and the announcement played, but before the "successfully spawned" log. Roles are already applied to the players.

events.notes: Roles is a get-only property but its dictionary contents are consumed, so mutating it is not a trap; Wave is read-only. Mutating the Roles dictionary (remove players, change roles, add players) IS honoured (it is rebuilt into the spawn dictionary); the maximum wave size still truncates afterwards. Roles is a POOLED dictionary: LabAPI releases it only on the allowed path, and its doc warns not to keep it. On cancel the SpawnQueue is cleared, players stay spectators, and the pooled Roles dictionary is not released (minor pool leak, UNVERIFIED impact). Player keys may be dummies/NPCs. Player.Get on the Roles keys can return a wrapper for hubs mid-disconnect (UNVERIFIED).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Fires once the wave is queued (state WaveSelected); the actual spawn happens later after the animation and countdown (RefreshNextWave), when WaveRespawning/WaveRespawned fire.

raisedFrom: WaveManager.InitiateRespawn (called from WaveManager.Update for a ready TimeBasedWave, and from RA/wave commands)
events.consumption: When allowed, the selected Wave is stored as the next wave and the state becomes WaveSelected; when cancelled none of that happens.
events.notes: TRAP: WaveManager.Update runs every frame. While the state is Idle it initiates the respawn for the first ready wave; if the handler cancels, the state stays Idle and the wave stays ready to spawn, so the event re-fires EVERY FRAME (per wave) until the wave stops being ready. Cancel only together with something that un-readies the wave (pause or reset its Timer, disable config). The Wave setter is consumed (the selected wave can be swapped). Args.Wave is the raw SpawnableWaveBase (not the LabAPI RespawnWave wrapper).

events.consumption: n/a (not cancellable, no setters)
events.notes: Raised after all WarheadDamageHandler kills were dealt (hub deaths already processed, PlayerEvents.Death/Dying for each victim fired earlier), SCP-244 destroyed, elevator doors locked and the shake RPC sent. Player is the host if there was no trigger.

raisedFrom: AlphaWarheadController.Detonate (called from ServerUpdateDetonationTime, which runs from Update every frame)
events.consumption: When cancelled the game returns; otherwise the trigger footprint is taken from Player.
events.notes: TRAP: Detonate is called every frame from ServerUpdateDetonationTime while the warhead has not yet detonated and the countdown is at zero or below. Cancelling leaves it not detonated and in progress, so the event re-fires EVERY FRAME (60/s) until the plugin cancels the warhead (CancelDetonation refuses at 10 s or less) or lets it through. Blast doors have already shut at under 2 s. Player is the trigger footprint hub or the host; setting Player to null causes a NullReferenceException.

raisedFrom: AlphaWarheadController.StartDetonation (callers: the button/RA path, which can suppress the subtitles, and the auto-nuke check every frame)
events.consumption: When cancelled the game returns; otherwise IsAutomatic, SuppressSubtitles, WarheadState and the trigger (from Player) are used.
events.notes: TRAP for the auto-nuke: its check runs every frame and starts the detonation automatically while auto-detonation is enabled, the warhead has not detonated or started, and the round time has reached the auto-detonation time; cancelling the automatic start therefore re-raises the event EVERY FRAME. Early-outs before the event: already in progress, cooldown, locked. Player is the host when there is no trigger (HostHub, not null); setting Player to null causes a NullReferenceException when the game reads its ReferenceHub. WarheadState (the AlphaWarheadSyncInfo struct including start time and scenario) is fully consumed.

events.notes: Raised after the network info (resume scenario) and the cooldown were set and the warhead-cancel door opener was triggered.
